transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I've been dealing with really bad hallucinations for a little over two years now. I keep hearing voices and seeing things that other people tell me aren't actually there. It's just getting really hard to cope with.
Along with these hallucinations, have you experienced any long periods of feeling extremely depressed or unusually energetic and active?
No, I haven't really experienced any long periods of feeling extremely depressed or unusually energetic. My mood has been mostly normal, aside from just feeling stressed out by the hallucinations.
Besides the hallucinations, have you had trouble with organizing your thoughts, expressing your feelings, or finding the motivation to do your normal daily activities?
No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of issues. My motivation is fine, and I don't have any trouble organizing my thoughts or expressing my feelings.
Have you had any strong beliefs or felt that people were spying on you, plotting against you, or that something unusual was happening, which others told you wasn't true?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I've never felt like anyone was spying on me or plotting against me, and my beliefs are pretty normal.
Have you been using any recreational drugs, alcohol, or prescription medications regularly during the time you've had these hallucinations?
No, I don't use any recreational drugs or drink alcohol. I haven't been taking any regular prescription medications during this time either.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any neurological or medical conditions, or have you ever experienced a significant head injury?
No, I've never been diagnosed with any neurological or medical conditions. I also haven't ever had a significant head injury.
How have these hallucinations affected your ability to work, maintain relationships, or manage your daily responsibilities over the past two years?

It has been really difficult and overwhelming trying to deal with all of this for over two years now. I'm not really sure how to describe the exact impact on my work, relationships, or daily life, though. Everything just feels a lot more stressful and hard to handle.

Yes, my family has noticed some strange behaviors. They've mentioned that I sometimes act really childish or silly in serious situations, or that I get suddenly agitated and make repetitive movements. It's something others have definitely pointed out to me.
Have others ever told you that your speech is difficult to follow, or that you jump from one topic to another in a way that doesn't make sense?
No, I don't think anyone has ever told me that. As far as I know, people can understand me just fine when I speak.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports prominent auditory and visual hallucinations for over two years, along with observed grossly disorganized behavior (acting childish/silly in serious situations, sudden agitation, and repetitive movements). They deny delusions, disorganized speech, and negative symptoms. They also deny any history of manic, hypomanic, or major depressive episodes, which rules out Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Disorders, and Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features. Delusional Disorder is ruled out due to the absence of delusions and the presence of prominent hallucinations and disorganized behavior. There is no history of substance use or medical/neurological conditions. The clinical picture meets the criteria for Schizophrenia.
